lawyer:
Mr. Md. Golam Mostafa with Mr. A.K.M. Rezaul Karim Khandaker, Advocates ------ For the Pre-emptee-Petitioner 
Mr. Humayun Kabir Sikder, Advocate ------ For the Opposite party No.1
parties:
Md. Ekram Hossain Bhuiyan
Vs.
Matiar Rahman Bhuiyan and others
full_judgment:
2. The material facts relevant for disposal of this Rule are that the Opposite Party No.1 as pre-emptor instituted pre-emption case No.65 of 1997 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Narail stating, inter-alia, that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer to the case jote by inheritance as well as by purchase while the pre-emptee is a stranger, who purchased the case land from his father by a registered kabala dated 14.12.1995 at the consideration of Tk. 12,000/-. It has been further asserted that his father Afsaruddin earlier gifted the case land verbally to him and after the death of Afsaruddin the pre-emptor came to learnt that his father has already been transferred the case land to the pre-emptee-petitioner. No notice of the said transfer in question was served upon the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 and hence the case on making the statutory deposit. 

 8. Mr. Md. Golam Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing for the pre-emptee-petitioner submits that the appellate Court below acted wrongly in holding that the pre-emptee purchaser is not a co-sharer in the tenancy and thereby illegally affirmed the decision of the trial Court. He next submits that both the Courts below erred in law in deciding the question of limitation in a casual manner without properly discussing and considering the evidence on this point and the same has resulted in an error in the impugned decisions occasioning failure of justice. He further adds that the father (Afsaruddin) of the pre-emptee petitioner as well as pre-emptor in presence of all his sons and daughters transferred the case land to the petitioner at the consideration of Tk. 12,000/- and rest 12 decimals of land have been possessing by the other heirs of Afsaruddin and the pre-emptee is the co-sharer in the tenancy with other heirs of Afsaruddin including the pre-emptor. Mr. Golam Mostafa, further submits that the application for pre-emption was barred by limitation inasmuch as the impugned deed was registered on 14.12.1995 and the pre-emption case was filed on 06.08.1997, after one year 8 months, though, before sale of the case land pre-emptor and pre-emptee, vendor and other co-sharers were present in the conversation regarding sale of suit land. The learned Advocate in the course of argument after placing the application for pre-emption and deposition of PWs. submits that the pre-emptor in his deposition stated that he learnt about the transfer in question after obtaining certified copy of the same on 01.06.1997 but PW 1 nowhere in his evidence disclosed that he came to know about the transfer in question for the first time on 01.06.1997. Mr. Golam Mostafa finally submits with force that the impugned judgments of both the Courts below based on non-consideration of the material evidence of the OPWs 1-3 who categorically testified that Afsaruddin, the father of the pre-emptee petitioner and pre-emptor within the full knowledge of all his sons and daughters including the pre-emptor transferred the case land to the petitioner by a registered kabala dated 14.12.1995 and as such impugned judgments of 2 (two) Courts below are liable to be set-aside. 

 12. PW-1, Matiar Rahman, as pre-emptor himself stated in his deposition that Shudhir, Dilip and Khokan transferred the land in question to his father on 13.05.1970 and his father while enjoying and possessing the land verbally gifted the land to him. This witness also stated in his deposition that after the death of his father on 18th Jaistha, 1404 B.S. he was asked to hand over the possession of the case land and thereafter on 01.06.97 after obtaining the certified copy of the impugned kabala he learnt about the transfer in question. He also stated that no transfer notice was served upon him. This witness in his cross-examination stated that: ১৪০৪ সালে বিক্রয়ের কথা জানি। ১৪০৪ সাল বাংলা না ইংরেজী তা বলতে পারবো না। বর্তমানে বাংলা কত সাল বলতে পারবো না। বাবা মারা যাওয়ার পর সম্পত্তি দখল করিতে আসে। একরাম তখন বিক্রয়ের কথা প্রকাশ করে। 

 13. PW-2, Akram Sheikh, stated in his deposition that the land in question was gifted by Afsaruddin Bhuiyan to his daughter's husband (pre-emptor). He also testified that he constructed a building on the case land. This witness in his cross-examination denied the suggestion that: সত্য নয় যে, দানের কাহিনী ও বাড়ী করার কাহিনী মিথ্যা। একরাম আর্মিতে চাকুরী করে ১৪০৪ সালের জৈষ্ঠ মাসে একরাম প্রকাশ করে। আমি বাংলা কোন সালে বিবাহ করি তা স্মরণ নাই। PW-3, Shamsul Haque Chowdhury, stated in his deposition that: মতিয়ার (pre-emptor)  আমাকে বলে যে, নালিশী জমি একরাম (pre-emptee) দলিল করে নেয়। কোন দাগের জমি বা কাহার নিকট থেকে লিখে নেয় সে সম্পর্কে আমাকে কিছু বলে নাই। কথা শুনে আমি চলে যাই। অন্য কোন বিষয়ে আমি জানি না। 

 14. On assessment of the evidence on record, it appears that PW-1, Matiar Rahman, as pre-emptor instituted the case on the allegation that his father Afsaruddin transferred the case land to his full bother OPW-1, Ekram Hossain, who was not a co-sharer to the case jote. It also appears that the deed in question was registered on 14.12.1995 and pre-emption case was filed on 06.08.1997, after one year 8 months. OPW-1, Ekram Hossain stated in his evidence that he purchased the case land from his father by a registered deed dated 14.12.1995. This witness also stated that : প্রার্থীসহ (pre-emptor) সকল ভাই বোনদের সম্মতিতে এই জমি খরিদ করি। OPW-2, Atiar Rahman, brother of the pre-emptor stated in his deposition that নালিশী জমি সহ ১.১০ একর জমি আমার পিতা খরিদ করে। তার মধ্যে ৯৮ শতক জমি একরামের (pre-emptee petitioner) নিকট বিক্রয় করে। বিক্রয়ের সময় প্রার্থীসহ আমরা সবাই ছিলাম। নালিশী জমির মধ্যে বাকী অংশ আমি বন্টন করি। This witness also stated that কথা বর্তার সময় আমরা ৫ ভাই ৫ বোন ও মাতা এবং করিম শেখ ছিল। বাবা বিক্রয়ের কথা বলে, বার হাজার টাকা দাম ঠিক হয়। OPW-3, Karim Sheikh, sister's husband of the pre-emptor stated in his deposition that: প্রার্থী প্রতিপক্ষ ও নালিশী জমি চিনি। আমার শ্বশুর ১.১০ একর জমি খরিদ করে। দখল করিত। তার মধ্যে ৯৮ শতক জমি একরামের (pre-emptee purchaser) নিকট বিক্রয় করে। এ বিষয়ে মতিয়ার (pre-emptor) সহ আমরা জানতাম। একরামের জমি আমরা দেখা শুনা করি। কিছু অংশ OPW-2 বর্গা করে। শ্বশুর মারা যাবার সময় ১২ শতক জমি খামার থাকে। এই জমি মতিয়ার পায়। 

 15. In the application for pre-emption, the pre-emptor has disclosed that he learnt about the transfer in question for the first time on 01.06.97. Pre-emptor himself as PW-1, stated in his testimony that after obtaining certified copy of the impugned kabala he came to know about the transfer in question on 01.06.97. This date of knowledge has not been corroborated by any other witnesses and the evidence of PW-1 without any corroboration cannot be accepted to record a finding that the pre-emptor has proved the date of his knowledge of the transfer in question. Therefore, I find merit in the submission of the of the learned Advocate, Mr. Md. Golam Mostafa that the pre-emptor did not prove the date of knowledge by adducing evidence and as such the application for pre-emption is barred by limitation since the deed in question was registered on 14.12.1995 and pre-emption case was filed on 06.08.1997, after one year 8 months. 

 16. Now let me examine the legal position in this regard. Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act clearly provides that a pre-emption application must be filed within 4 months form the date of registration of the deed or within 4 months from the date of knowledge of the transfer in question where notice under section 89 is not served. The burden of proof that the application has been filed within 4 months of the date knowledge of the transfer heavily lies upon the applicant. 

 17. There is another aspect of the case. Both the Courts bellow arrived at a concurrent finding that the pre-emptee was not a co-sharer in the tenancy. It is not disputed that Afsaruddin (father of the pre-emptor and pre-emptee) had become co-sharer in the tenancy by purchase form the three original co-sharers, who transferred the case land to his son (pre-emptee -petitioner) by a registered kabala dated 14.12.1995. On consideration of the entire materials on record, it appears to me that the pre-emptor and/he pre-emptee are co-sharers by inheritance, to be on equal footing. 

 18. Be that as it may, provisions for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 is not applicable to a transfer in favour of a co-sharer whose interest in the tenancy has accrued by inheritance. In this case the transfer under the kabala dated 14.12.1995 was made to this petitioner by his father is protected and immune from the pre-emption under sub-section 10(a) to section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act inasmuch as the pre-emptee's interest in the tenancy has accrued by inheritance simply because the pre-emptee inherited his father's share. 

 20. The pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 mentioned in the application for pre-emption that his father Afsaruddin earlier gifted the case land verbally to him. It appears that the pre-emptor as PW-1, stated in his evidence that: বাবা আকরাম কে দলিল করিয়া দেয় নাই সেই কারনে আমার দানমুলে কোন দাবী নাই। In that view of the matter, I need not embark upon detail discussion on this point.
